newsitem.title: CHINA: China newspaper urges curbs on automobile industry.
newsitem.headline: China newspaper urges curbs on automobile industry.

text.p: A Chinese newspaper on Tuesday called for an end to blind investment by provinces in automobile manufacturing and urged mergers of small factories to streamline the industry.
The structure of the domestic automobile industry was "unreasonable", it said, with too many small firms and too few large enterprises.

In 1985 the authorities ordered the closure of automobile plants with low efficiency and poor management, but more than 10 years later, the number of firms had increased sharply due to blind investment by many provinces, the newspaper said.
China now had 838 automobile enterprises in 27 provinces, the highest number in the world, it said.
Domestic vehicle output in 1995 was just 1.5 million units, less than one-fifth of the annual production of General Motors Corp of the United States, it said.
China has just four automobile firms with annual production capacity of more than 100,000 vehicles and more than 10 firms with capacity of over 10,000, it said.
The newspaper said China should set up several large-scale automobile groups by merging small firms to upgrade technology and efficiency. It did not give further details.
Car prices have fallen steadily in the past year amid overproduction and lack of demand, prompting several foreign manufacturers in joint ventures to review their investment.
